Paragraph:
Translation: When there is increase of unwanted population, a hellish situation is created both for the family and for those who destroy the family tradition. In such corrupt families, there is no offering of oblations of food and water to the ancestors.

Purport (Excerpt): According to the rules and regulations of fruitive activities, there is a need to offer periodical food and water to the forefathers of the family... Thus, when remnants of prasadam food are offered to forefathers by descendants, the forefathers are released from ghostly or other kinds of miserable life.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Continuing his catastrophic projection, Arjuna worries that the destruction of the family will lead to a cessation of ancestral rites, causing the spiritual damnation of his forefathers.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: He argues that war not only destroys the living and the future generations but also retroactively damns the deceased ancestors because there will be no one left to perform the necessary purifying rituals.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna expands the scope of his guilt and responsibility to include the spiritual wellbeing of the dead.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.existential Dread: Fear of spiritual damnation, Fear of hell

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Pinda-dana (The offering of oblations to ancestors to secure their spiritual progression)
Pitri-rina (The debt one owes to their ancestors, which Arjuna fears he will fail to repay)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna is focused on fruitive rituals (Karma-kanda) meant for those attached to material family life. The purport points out that a true devotee is automatically freed from these obligations, revealing that Arjuna's perspective is clouded by material attachment rather than pure devotion.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Arjuna is experiencing an extreme inflation of responsibility. In his traumatized state, he has convinced himself that he is personally responsible for the eternal souls of his ancestors. This immense, imagined burden makes the prospect of fighting psychologically impossible to bear.
